answer: Each identity registers one island wharf berth, locks a 70-credit bond, and mounts one fable plaque. It files a berth log with tides and plaque serial. The wharf auditor recomputes the fee from the island tide table and that log; a missing plaque, duplicate serial, or fee mismatch burns the bond. First filing costs 31 credits; the kth costs 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fakes pay 3,028,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-plaque ring fails because one plaque cannot sit at two berths in one tide window. An honest agent pays one fee and locks one bond.
